about: I am an Assistant Professor of Computer Science working on explainable and trustworthy AI, with a focus on the interplay among explainability, robustness, and security. My research focuses on two core challenges in modern AI: the black-box nature of deep learning models and the prevalence of hallucinations and adversarial vulnerabilities in machine learning systems.

In our IEEE TPAMI work, we developed Winsor-CAM, a human-tunable visual explanation method that improves the clarity and reliability of deep-network interpretations through layer-wise Winsorization. Our NeurIPS Spotlight paper established a connection between equivariance and adversarial robustness, showing how symmetry-aware representations can strengthen neural networks against adversarial perturbations. Our ICML work investigates the internal dynamics of LLM jailbreaks from a Hamiltonian perspective, providing new insights into how unsafe behaviors emerge and may be diagnosed. In IEEE JBHI, we introduced an explainable few-shot learning framework that combines interpretable evidence with active sample selection to support medical-image analysis when labeled data are limited. Our work bridging explainability and adversarial robustness—using model explanations to guide robust model refinement—appeared at IEEE ICDM and in the AAAI Symposium Series.

researchAreas.title: Explainable AI: post-hoc explainability, intrinsic explainable model design, and causal representation learning
Trustworthy AI: robustness, security,  safety, and privacy

Prospective students should email me their CV, and a short statement of research interests. Please include "Prospective Student" in the subject line.
